kind: pinned conjuncts: hand-written assertions about the LIVE registries
why: RC-02. The criterion-content oracle compares predicate-registry.json to tools/phase_content.py and fails on any difference -- which makes a HAND edit of a criterion a failing build, and makes a DERIVATION edit invisible. The recheck measured it: one hunk replacing the ('SalesAgreement','performed') spec, then `python3 tools/author_phase_content.py`, and the whole G2-01 defect is back at exit 0, 268,829 checks, with all 27 negative fixtures still rejecting. A checker that compares an artifact to a source the same author controls is not a checker. Every assertion below is written BY HAND against the live registry and is never generated from anything: author_phase_content.py does not read this file and cannot write it, so regenerating the registry from a weakened derivation now fails HERE, naming the conjunct that went missing. RC2-02, the same argument one operator over and found the same way -- by mutation, not by reading: these rows asserted CONTAINMENT, and a conjunct kept verbatim inside an `any` beside a trivially-true alternative is contained by the body while being demanded by nothing. Every `why` below is written as a demand, so each row now says which it means: `disjoined` defaults to false and the four rows whose requirement really is conditional name their branch.

how_to_read.pin: one predicate id, the findings and decisions that put each requirement there, and the `require` rows that must hold of its body in the committed predicate-registry.json
how_to_read.matching: a row matches when SOME node of the body carries that `op` and satisfies every constraint on the row. Structural containment only: a body may carry more than is pinned, never less.
how_to_read.negated: false (the default) requires a matching node that is NOT beneath a `not`; true requires one that IS. Without this, wrapping a pinned conjunct in `not` would satisfy a containment check while inverting the requirement.
how_to_read.disjoined: false (the default) requires a matching node that is NOT beneath an `any`: the body must DEMAND the conjunct, not merely mention it in one branch of a disjunction. true permits a match inside one, for a requirement that is genuinely conditional, and then `disjoined_why` must name the condition. RC2-02 is why it exists and it was measured, not argued: disjoining each of the three pinned conjuncts of criterion.SalesAgreement.performed.v1 with `present(/payload/agreed_terms)` -- a field records.schema.json already requires of every SalesAgreement -- left every pin matching, this file untouched, and validate_contracts.py at exit 0 with 31 of 31 negative fixtures still rejecting, over a criterion that demanded none of it. Four rows opt in; each names its branch. Disjunction is read through negation rather than beside it, because `not(any(A, B))` demands `not A` while `not(all(A, B))` demands neither.
how_to_read.disjoined_why: required on a row with `disjoined: true` and REFUSED on any other row. An opt-out of the demand rule states which condition makes the requirement conditional, in the same way `unpinnable` states why no conjunct can carry a finding: an excuse nobody had to write is an excuse nobody reads.
how_to_read.states_exactly: the binding's `states` list must equal this set. A superset is a weakening -- `['delivered','proposed']` admits the exact counterexample AD-013 was decided to refuse -- and a subset is a different requirement than the one recorded.
how_to_read.closed_key_set: validate_contracts.py declares the constraint keys it reads and REFUSES any other key in a row. A pin whose constraint the checker silently ignored would be the same defect one layer up: a control that reads as enforcement while nothing checks it.

checked_by: validate_contracts.py: each pin against predicate-registry.json directly, with no import of tools/phase_content.py
validate_contracts.py: coverage -- every finding id swept out of registers/review-findings.json is pinned here or declared in `unpinnable` with a reason
fixtures/negative/r13-derivation-weakened-then-regenerated: patches tools/phase_content.py, regenerates with author_phase_content.py, and must be REJECTED by these pins

fixtures/negative/r14-pinned-conjunct-disjoined-with-a-tautology: disjoins each pinned conjunct of criterion.SalesAgreement.performed.v1 with a tautology, regenerates with author_phase_content.py, and must be REJECTED naming the disjunction -- r13-derivation-weakened-then-regenerated cannot catch this, because it REMOVES the conjuncts rather than weakening them
admissible_ancestors_why: RC4-02, and it is the structural rule this whole block now turns on: A REGISTRY MAY CLASSIFY POSITIONS; ONLY THIS FILE MAY SAY WHAT SATISFIES ONE. RC3-01's repair moved the definition of "demanded" out of a hard-coded triple in validate_contracts.py and into primitive-registry.json's `argument_positions` -- which the derivation's author also writes. The fourth recheck measured what that bought: register a NEW primitive `every_linked_obligation` with `argument_types.predicate: "boolean"` and `argument_positions.predicate: "demanded"`, wrap the three pinned conjuncts of criterion.SalesAgreement.performed.v1 in it, regenerate -- and the tree passes at exit 0 with 288,665 checks and 36 of 36 negative fixtures still rejecting, over a registry in which those conjuncts sit inside a quantifier over `/payload/obligation_refs`, a field records.schema.json gives no `minItems`. G2-01's counterexample, restored by a primitive that declared itself demanding. The table was closed against the UNDECLARED and open to the MISDECLARED. This table closes the second half: a pinned conjunct counts as demanded only when EVERY operator it sits inside, through a slot the registry calls a predicate position, is named here -- whatever `argument_positions` says about that operator. A primitive that declares its own child demanded and is not named here refuses the match, and the message names the operator.

all.why: The conjunction. A child of `all` is true exactly when the body is, so a pinned conjunct sitting inside one is demanded with no condition. Measured over the committed corpus: every chain of demand-bearing ancestors of a matched pin row is drawn from `all`, `not` and `any` and from nothing else -- 3,318 of the RC-03 walk's positions sit under `('all',)` alone -- so this table costs no live match today and refuses every operator a future author could add.

not.why: Negation is admissible because its whole effect on demand is POLARITY, and the row already states its polarity: `negated: true` requires a match beneath an odd number of `not`s and the default requires one beneath an even number. The containment filter in validate_contracts.py compares the two before this rule runs, so this entry is a backstop over that filter rather than the live control -- stated plainly, because a declaration whose condition nothing evaluates is the RC4 class one layer up. For a pinned VALUE op polarity is not a question at all (`path` and `resolve` return a JsonValue), and one live row matches a `path` reached through `eq.left` beneath `('all','any','not')`; `row_polarity` admits it for that reason and not by accident.

any.why: RC2-02's operator, and the only CONDITIONAL entry here. A conjunct kept verbatim in one branch of an `any` is contained by the body and demanded by nothing, so an `any` ancestor is admissible only for a row that opted in with `disjoined: true` and named its branch in `disjoined_why`. Four rows do, and the ceiling of four in validate_contracts.py is what stops a fifth arriving quietly. Read `admits` honestly: this condition and `not`'s are BACKSTOPS. The ancestor rule runs over the entries that would already satisfy the row, which the disjunction and polarity filters shaped first, so neither condition can fail on a tree those filters passed. MEMBERSHIP in this table is the live control; the conditions are written and evaluated so that the table states its reasons in something a checker reads rather than in prose.

admissible_ancestors_not_admitted.forall: The registry's fourth boolean-child primitive, and RC3-01's route. `quantified` is unconditionally non-demanding here: a `forall` over a collection nothing forces non-empty is vacuously true, and nothing in this corpus forces any collection non-empty. Deliberately NOT given a conditional entry -- see RC4-04 and the note the quantifier refusal prints. Demanding the collection non-empty on a sibling conjunct does NOT lift the rule.
admissible_ancestors_not_admitted.anything else: Any primitive not named in `admissible_ancestors` -- including one registered tomorrow that declares its own `boolean` child `demanded`. That is RC4-02, and it is the reason this table is a closed set of NAMES rather than a rule over roles.

argument_positions_digest_why: RC4-01. `primitive-registry.json` is written by tools/author_phase_content.py, tools/repair_r2_bootstrap_root.py and tools/repair_r3_intrinsic_subjects.py, and before this line nothing asserted a byte of it: the criterion-content drift oracle never compares the file, the guard ratchet only budgets sibling collisions, and there was no hash anywhere in the package. The fourth recheck flipped ONE string -- `/forall/argument_positions/predicate` from `"quantified"` to `"demanded"` -- and the vacuous-`forall` body validated at 288,646 checks with every pin satisfied, the census still reporting `under_quantifier: 0` because the census reads the same table. The only thing that refused it was a negative fixture naming `forall` by hand, and the sentence it printed named the FIXTURE rather than the table. This digest is sha256 over `{name: argument_positions}` for every primitive, sorted keys, compact separators, and it is MAINTAINED BY HAND: any edit to any argument position of any primitive fails the build until someone writes the new digest here, which is a line in a diff a reviewer sees. Recompute it with: python3 -c "import json,hashlib; p=json.load(open('primitive-registry.json')); print(hashlib.sha256(json.dumps({k:v['argument_positions'] for k,v in sorted(p.items())},sort_keys=True,separators=(',',':')).encode()).hexdigest())"

unpinnable.why: A coverage finding about what the specification chapters SAY, closed by prose in the residue lane. No predicate expresses it, so a conjunct pin would be a pin on something else wearing its id.
This file IS the repair for RC-02. Pinning a conjunct 'for RC-02' would be circular; what enforces it is the coverage check below plus fixtures/negative/r13-derivation-weakened-then-regenerated.

A check on the relation between a criterion's `requires` sentence and its conjuncts, which is a property of every criterion rather than of any one predicate. Implemented in validate_contracts.py as the requires/conjuncts agreement check.
A property of the negative-fixture suite, not of the registry. Implemented as fixtures/negative/MANIFEST.json and the count ratchet in tools/run_negative_fixtures.py.
A property of how the runner resolves its own root. Implemented as the symlink refusal in tools/run_negative_fixtures.py.
A prose gap: `terminated_with_residuals` appears in no specification chapter. The phase-meaning row in chapter 03 closes it; no conjunct can.

pins.why: G4-08: the schema omitted `competence_requirement_ref` from `required` while this criterion demanded it, so two implementers derive different packets from one contract -- and the stricter reading destroyed the case DIRECTIVE.md §1.6 most wants preserved, a pure taste decision with no competence prerequisite to name.

the dependency graph over the children is acyclic -- a packet that is its own prerequisite is `ready` under any evidence rule

require.why: either burden was observed, or the account states `none_observed` with a reason, a window and a responsible assignment. Deleting the second disjunct restores the silent `[]`; deleting the first makes observation unrecordable.

a currently accepted performer delivered it

A conjunct removed for a stated reason is one removal away from the next one having no reason at all, so what REMAINS is pinned: the failure is owned, not merely declared.

require.why: the obligations survive on the record, and the receipts actually obtained and the window are recorded -- a failure that recorded none of these would be a closure wearing the word failure
CAP-30: failure creates a support/remedy duty, and a duty with no accepted performer is unowned

pins.why: G4-02: `remedy_reservation_refs` was required in the payload and used by 0 predicates, and this criterion carried `nonempty_fields: []` -- so a remedy could be authorized with no reservation at all, which is what made CAP-42's funded remedy prose.

pins.why: G4-01: `disputed_custodian` is required on GrievanceCase and was read by 0 of 2,255 predicates. The criterion carries the two refs the guard's `neq` compares; erase them here and the comparison one layer up compares absent fields.

require.why: both sides of the conflict-of-interest comparison must be recorded at triage
the custodian has accepted the case

pins.why: The original (d): `performed` demanded byte-identical field_paths to `accepted`, the agreement had no relation to a Fulfillment, and the only native object reachable was the payment -- so a buyer could pay, the Fulfillment stay `proposed`, every Obligation stay `recognized`, and the sale reach `performed` with nothing objecting. pins.why: The GrantDeliveryReceipt guarantee, pinned where it binds: an executor whose grant did not arrive fails loudly and never completes with less. It is stated on the edge that starts the executor rather than in a guard, because the thirty guard names of section 12.4 are a closed list and this guarantee is not one of them.

Listing the nine closure edges explicitly rather than generating four is why this one is here.

pins.why: The writer guard on the terminal acceptance edge. Producer-declared completion is not acceptance, and an acceptance with no resolution reason is an interval that timed out wearing a decision's name.

require.why: the reason and the owner who wrote it are both on the record
the reason is non-empty as a value, not merely present as a key
and it is not the empty string. Two rows for one requirement because `present`, `nonempty` and `!= ""` fail on three different shapes of the same evasion

pins.why: R-X09 and R-D09: every acceptance-owner role is a record, and admission in that duty class STOPS while it is unfilled. The mechanism is closed here; who is staffed is the founder's (MD-02).

require.why: the duty class and the holder that accepts in it are both named on the admission
that holder is CURRENTLY `staffed`. `optional: true` here would readmit the whole finding with the field simply absent, which is what admission-narrowing exists to refuse

pins.why: A refusal is a terminal state of the admission record with a named failed predicate and its own acceptance owner. Silence is not refusal. The third row is the FALSE-EXCLUSION control (05 section 9, row 17): the basis of a refusal is a failed predicate, so a genuine job in wording the catalogue does not recognise types as no_match -- a searched answer -- rather than being refused.

require.why: a refusal names the predicate that failed AND the party who accepts the refusal
and that predicate id is not the empty string, which is how a required field becomes a formality
the BASIS of the refusal is a failed predicate. Unfamiliar wording is not a predicate: this is the row that stops the refusal path swallowing work it merely did not recognise

pins.why: R-X18: every approval carries an expiry, and the monotonic-exposure diff is over effects releasable without a human. Each approval is individually small and the ratchet lives only in their sum, which is the object an executor's own record never shows.

require.why: an approval and its expiry are both on the record; an approval with no expiry is a permanent one
and the expiry is strictly after the approval, so an expiry set to the approval instant is not an expiry

pins.why: R-X19. Procedure admission refuses a branch set in which a model-authored value selects between acceptance strengths for one artifact. Acceptance-strength selection is a guard over journal state and consequence class, never a jump a model's output takes.

require.why: the selector is one of the two admitted kinds, read off the declared branch set
and it is explicitly not a model. Stated twice on purpose: the allow-list is the rule and this is the sentence a reader of the diff sees

pins.why: R-X20. A check interest's precondition reads ONLY fields the producer could not author; a check that reads an authorable field is a check the producer can arm and disarm.

require.why: what the check reads and what the producer cannot author are both declared as path lists
everything the check reads is inside the non-authorable set. Reversing the direction is the finding

pins.why: The other half of R-X20: the tie-break for CHECK interests inverts to strongest sufficient, because the cheapest sufficient check is the one an adversary arms.

require.why: the tie-break rule is strongest-sufficient, declared as a value rather than left to the resolver's default

pins.why: The rule is NEGATIVE -- no total rank and no severity score is computed from the reached set -- and a negative rule needs something positive to check. The derivation declares its ordering as `none` and a guard reads that declaration; a future implementer who reintroduces a rank has to change this literal, which is a line in a diff someone sees.

require.why: the derivation declares NO ordering over the reached set; any other value is a rank by another name
a set, not a list: a repeated class id is how a count-based gate check gets fooled

pins.why: AT-M4-02 measured the collapse: an action that is both C2 and C3, gated only by the higher row, loses C2's human requirement. The repair is that the gate evaluator consumes the SET, and these three rows ARE that -- the reached ids and the gated ids are both named, every reached class is inside the gated set, and the two are the same size, so gating a proper subset is not a smaller version of gating the set.

require.why: both sides must be NAMED on the record; without them the two comparisons below bind to nothing
every class the derivation reached is in the gated set -- this is 'every reached class's gates apply', stated as a predicate
and the two sets are the same size, so a gate set that covers only the highest reached class fails here rather than passing the containment above

pins.why: The containment that makes layer 3 safe to compute: an interest arms and proposes; it never admits. Its write targets are a subset of the proposed phase, checked rather than described.

require.why: every phase this interest may write into is `proposed`. Widening this list is how an interest becomes an admitter

pins.why: The other half of AS-X-01. Freezing criteria the producing path authored freezes the wrong thing, so the author is required to be outside the producing path by membership rather than by intent.

require.why: the author and the producing path are both named as ids, which is what makes the membership test mechanical
the author is NOT a member of the producing path. The polarity is the requirement: drop the negation and the guard demands the opposite of what the finding asked for

pins.why: AS-X-01, resolved by R-D11: the capability owner authors the acceptance criteria and they are frozen BEFORE the producing step starts. This closes the fourth unblinded channel into the checker, which no research lane named and one review found.

require.why: the criteria, the moment they froze and the moment production started are all on the record, so the ordering below is checkable rather than asserted
frozen STRICTLY BEFORE production started; equality would admit criteria written in the same act as the work they judge

pins.why: R-X06. The prohibition 'the admitter may not accept work it admitted' yields a mechanism rather than a sentence: the ordered custody resolver SKIPS the admitting identity and continues to the next tier.

require.why: the admitting identity and the ordered custody list are both on the record, which is what makes the exclusion checkable
the admitting identity is NOT in the resolved custody order. Polarity is the rule here

pins.why: R-X16. Fifty sequential consultations, each individually cheap, sit inside one budget and are a fan-out incident. The ceiling is therefore over DISTINCT READ SETS rather than over cost, with the same owner and checkpoint as the depth ceiling.

require.why: the read sets seen so far and the ceiling are both on the attempt
the COUNT of distinct read sets is at most the ceiling. Replacing this with a cost comparison is the finding
and the digests are distinct, so fifty consultations over one read set count once and fifty over fifty count fifty

pins.why: A boundary is real only if what is checked at the moment of the effect is what was granted. `matched` is the phase that asserts the recomputation agreed with the admitted set, so the guard on that edge must compare the two sets and not merely observe that a recomputation happened.

require.why: both sets are named on the record before either is compared
nothing the release-time recomputation reached is outside the admitted set
and the sets are the same size, so a recomputation that reached MORE cannot take this edge -- it parks, and a park never resolves downward

F6D-03, and this is AT-M4-02's harm through the recompute path. reached=[C2,C3] against recomputed=[C3,C3] satisfies the containment and the count equality above, so the record reaches `matched`, the release proceeds, and C2's human requirement on an outward disclosure is gone. `parked_on_mismatch` -- the phase whose row reads "it never resolves downward" -- is simply not entered. Duplicate-free on the recomputed side is what makes the count comparison mean set size.

and on the admitted side. The sibling guard `guard.class.reached_set_gates_all` uses the identical idiom and is safe only because it shares an edge with `guard.class.no_total_rank`, which asserts `unique` on this field. This guard sits on the NEXT edge, where no guard asserted it at all.

pins.why: R-L1's writer clause. The derivation record is written only inside the release path and is append-only; an executor's grant scope is a proposal right and C04 performs every release (R-X01).

require.why: the release path, named as a component id rather than implied by who happened to write it
append-only: a derivation that can be rewritten is a boundary that can be moved after the fact

pins.why: The identity triple is complete and allocated BEFORE release, by C04. A second claimant joins the first and inherits its outcome; without an identity allocated first there is nothing for it to join.

require.why: the whole identity triple plus the moment of allocation; a partial triple correlates two different effects
allocation strictly precedes the claim -- allocated BEFORE release is the ordering, not a field that happens to be filled in
and C04 allocated it, which is the component that performs every release

pins.why: R-L2: one effect per effect step, and the step boundary is the checkpoint, so the step is the idempotency unit. Two effects in one step have one journal position between them and no way to resume between them.

require.why: at most ONE effect reference per step
and the declared idempotency unit is the step, so a retry replays the same boundary

pins.why: AE-M4-01: four protected holders that could each refuse a shed can hold an empty bucket hostage with no override anywhere. A holder may negotiate and never veto, and its pre-declared minimum is EVIDENCE rather than consent.

require.why: the holder carries no veto right. Flipping this to true is the finding, restored
and its stated minimum is recorded AS evidence, so a shed records it and proceeds rather than waiting on it

pins.why: Retirement is refused while any duty the holder carries is live, and the successor that inherits the address and the residual duties is named. A closure that completed while a grievance route was unowned is a broken promise recorded as a clean end.

require.why: the holder this one retires INTO is named; retiring into nothing is the unowned route
and no duty it holds is still live

pins.why: AS-M2-01: an adversary filing many well-formed complaints through the published route exhausts the cap, and the next write -- from a legitimate complainant -- is refused at exactly the object whose purpose is to guarantee an outside party can always reach someone. R-X17: the cap overflows to a named destination with an alarm and a reader; it never refuses intake.

require.why: both sub-caps, the overflow destination and the READER of its alarm. A destination nobody reads is a queue nobody polls, which this chapter names as a silent-drop shape
and intake was not refused. This is the row that distinguishes R-X17's repair from the design it repairs

pins.why: R-L3's hardest line: NO precondition may invoke a model. Arming is a computed, unstoppable set evaluated by deterministic code over typed fields after every committed transition, and a model in a precondition makes the set neither computed nor unstoppable.

require.why: the evaluator is deterministic, declared as a value a guard can read
and it is explicitly not a model -- the prohibition stated as its own conjunct, because an allow-list widened by one entry is a quieter change than a deleted refusal

pins.why: AS-M5-02: a trial interest declaring a writer key over an existing sole-writer kind takes custody of a kind by asserting it. An interest declares no writer key of its own, and writer-key authority comes from outside it.

require.why: the self-declared writer key list is EMPTY. `[]` rather than absent: an absent field is a field nobody looked at
and the authority for any writer key it uses is external to the interest

pins.why: AS-X-02 names the asymmetry: three candidates gave grant DELIVERY a positive control and none gave grant REMOVAL one. This is that control -- a probe skill that declares a tool grant, whose ARRIVAL at the enforcement point is the failure. A stripper that has never been observed to strip is a stripper nobody has seen work.

require.why: the probe and its result are both recorded; a control with no recorded reading is a control nobody ran
the probe's declared grant was ABSENT at the enforcement point. This literal is the whole positive control
and it did not arrive. Stated as its own conjunct because the failing reading is the one a reader must be able to find by name

pins.why: AD-017: a step declares its read set and the loader delivers and RECORDS it. That converts 'the checker did not read the producer's rationale' from an assertion into a manifest fact. The equality is checked against the loader's own record, never against the caller's claimed read list.

require.why: the loader's record carries BOTH what was asked for and what it actually delivered
nothing declared went undelivered -- the half that catches a starved step
and nothing UNDECLARED was delivered -- the half that catches the producer's rationale field arriving in a checker's inputs, which is section 9's adverse row 2

F6D-02. A READ SET IS A SET. `subset` is element-wise and `count` counts duplicates, so declared=["/artifact","/artifact"] against delivered=["/artifact","/producer_rationale"] satisfies both rows above -- the producer's rationale reaches the checker while the loader's own record certifies that it did not. Duplicate-free on both sides, plus the containment and the count equality, IS set equality; this is the half that closes it on the declared side.

and on the delivered side, for the same reason in the other direction. Pin 34 on `guard.class.no_total_rank` had already written the sentence -- "a set, not a list: a repeated class id is how a count-based gate check gets fooled" -- and the idiom was not swept: six guards use `subset`, two pair it with a count to mean set equality, and neither of those two carried `unique` until now.

pins.why: R-X24 and AD-022: a reserve under a non-rolling allowance is waste rather than thrift, so reserved-but-unconsumed allowance lapses at the declared point INDEPENDENTLY of the holder's consent, and the quantity that lapsed is recorded per lane per window.

require.why: the lapse point is declared on the reservation rather than decided under pressure
the lapse does NOT require the holder's consent. This is the whole of AD-022's second half
and the quantity that lapsed unconsumed is recorded -- an unrecorded lapse is the waste nobody can price

pins.why: R-X15. A skill's declared tool grant is INERT: the launcher computes the tool set from the work order's grant and strips tool-granting frontmatter. Content-hash pinning is re-checked at USE rather than at install, because a stale borrowed skill passes shape checks.

require.why: the skill's own declared grant grants nothing
and the tool set comes from the work order, which is the only place a grant is authorised
the content hash is re-checked at use; a hash checked only at install pins a file that has since moved

pins.why: R-G06. Superseding an entry walks the transitive closure of derived entries naming the superseded value and re-decides or flags each reopened acceptance. The `present` rows rather than `nonempty` rows are deliberate: a supersession with an EMPTY closure must reopen nothing and must pass, which is section 9's benign row 11.

require.why: the closure was computed -- present even when empty, because an absent closure and an empty one are different facts
and what it reopened was recorded, likewise present even when empty
the walk ran to completion; a partial walk reports an empty closure that looks exactly like a real one
every acceptance reopened came from the closure, so the reopen set cannot be authored beside the walk

pins.why: R-X13. Per-item trust level is a required manifest field, and a derived item's level is the FLOOR of its inputs': deriving from an untrusted entry cannot launder it into a trusted one.

require.why: per-item levels are a manifest field, not a per-record one, and both sides of the floor are recorded
the derived level IS the minimum input level; anything else is a promotion, which the guard below governs

pins.why: AS-M5-01: an untrusted entry promoted to attested by the investigating activation is the activation reading its own output back as corroboration. Promotion is an effect with a discriminator that is not a model, and the corroborant is out of band.

require.why: the discriminator is not a model. This is the row the finding is about
and the rule names the out-of-band corroborant, so a promotion sourced from the investigating path has no route through this guard

pins.why: A declared grant is RESOLVED at admission, not recorded. The two rows are the two halves of that: the list is on the record, and every ref in it currently stands at `active` in the Grant registry -- which IS the grant policy, because a second grant-policy record would be a second authority over one question. Arrival is a different fact from scope: `grant_arrival_attested` on the lease edge attests that a grant arrived, never that it was the right one, and this is the half that checks scope.

require.why: the declaration is present and not empty; an empty list would satisfy any resolution rule vacuously, which is how the field read as enforcement while nothing read it

and every ref in it resolves to a Grant standing at `active`. `optional: false` is the load-bearing half -- with it optional, a declaration that resolves to nothing passes, which is the state the field was in.

pins.why: The guard carries the PHASE half of the rule and the schema carries the PRESENCE half, and they are stated in different places on purpose. Phase: any protected change this subject names stands at `authorized`, `staged`, `activated` or `verified` -- `proposed` and `reviewed` are excluded because reviewed means an assessment completed and authorized means a competent decision was taken, and it is the decision the rule is about. `rejected`, `rollback_required` and `rolled_back` are excluded for the obvious reason. Presence: `protected_change_ref` is `required` on ConsequenceClassDefinition, FieldAuthority and StandingHolder, whose listed transitions are always control-object changes, and on ConfigurationVersion it is required by `dependentRequired` exactly when `control_object_kind` is declared -- which is what keeps the paired benign case, an ordinary configuration admitted normally, from being refused. The binding is therefore `optional: true` HERE and must not be read as an escape: it is the one place where a record may legitimately name no protected change, and PS-CONTROL-OBJECT-CONDITIONAL in validate_contracts.py is what stops that place widening.

require.why: a named protected change stands at authorized or later. Detached or weakened to `proposed`, a floor changes on the strength of a proposal nobody decided.

pins.why: The join, stated as a predicate. The triple is named on the record -- it is the natural key declared in `EffectIdentity.identity`, so two allocations of one triple are one allocation -- and the claim names the operation intent whose outcome it inherits, which must already stand at `released` or `observed`. `optional: false` is what makes the second row bind: with it optional, a claim naming nothing passes and the inheritance is a sentence again. What this repair does NOT add is an exclusive-factory command: the nine records that declare one name a command in a registry with its own generated schema, and three of those nine name a command the command registry does not contain at all -- a pre-existing gap, recorded here rather than widened.

require.why: the business triple and the first claimant are all named on the record before the claim is judged; the triple is the declared natural key and the claimant is what the inheritance points at
and the first claimant already released or was observed, so there is an outcome to inherit. A claim cannot invent one, which is the difference between joining and re-releasing.

pinned_transitions_why:
A conjunct pin holds a guard to what it must DEMAND. It says nothing about whether the edge exists at all, and RC-01 was exactly that shape of defect: every guard was well formed, every criterion was sourced, and a delivery that failed in flight had nowhere to go. Deleting a transition is a one-line edit to record-registry.json that no check in this package noticed -- phase reachability is not checked, and a phase with fewer ways in is not a phase with fewer conjuncts. These rows are hand-written for the same reason the conjunct pins are: nothing derives them, so regenerating cannot satisfy them.

F6D-04 extends this table from 6 rows to 32. The six it had were all on `Fulfillment` and `SalesAgreement`, and NOT ONE of the fifteen WORK-1.1 records had a pinned transition -- so the earlier repair pinned the instances it found and the new layer arrived with none. Measured: three edge deletions, `ConsequenceDerivation: recomputed_at_release -> parked_on_mismatch`, `AcceptanceInterval: in_acceptance -> rejected` and `StandingHolder: staffed -> suspended`, three validator runs, three exit 0. Every edge named in `pinned_attachments` is pinned here as well, because the two attacks are different: deleting the CALL leaves the route and removes the check, deleting the TRANSITION leaves the check and removes the route, and each control is blind to the other's attack.

pinned_transitions.why: A delivery that fails IN FLIGHT. Without this edge `delivering` exits only to `delivered` or `superseded`, so the only route to `failed` runs through a delivery that was correlated -- which is the contradiction RC-01 names.
Refunding an undelivered sale -- the commonest refund there is -- was unrepresentable while `refunded` had one inbound edge, from `delivered`.
The other half of the same requirement: `refunded` is reachable from BOTH, and a repair that added one route by deleting the other would satisfy a looser reading of the finding.
RC-08: without it the generic validation branch and the delivery branch are disjoint, so a validated Fulfillment can only be delivered by a route that skipped validation.
The edge AD-013's delivery evidence hangs on. Its conjuncts are pinned above; this pins that there is an edge for them to be conjuncts OF.
The route OUT of residuals. Without it `terminated_with_residuals` is a terminal state that keeps its duties forever, which is a different contract from the one AD-014 decided.

requires_waivers_why: RC-03. `requires` and `conjuncts` are independent fields of one spec and nothing compared them, so a criterion could state one requirement and demand another -- which is what the weakened derivation produced: the sentence still promised delivery over a body that had stopped asking for it. Measured before any waiver: 774 criteria examined, 0 failing the field-path rule, 17 failing the phase-name rule, every one of the 17 a phase-kind synonym for the criterion's OWN phase. Each waiver below names the exact tokens it excuses, so a new unmatched phase on a waived criterion still fails. SCOPE, stated because the rule's name promises more than the rule does (RC2-03). What is compared is a FORMATTING-DEPENDENT SUBSET of the sentence: backticked lowercase tokens (PROSE_TOKEN) and field paths that are either backticked or written literally as /payload/... (PROSE_PATH). English nouns are not compared to conjuncts, and most of what these sentences are made of is English nouns. Removing three pairs of backticks leaves a sentence promising a reader exactly the same thing and invisible to the rule -- the recheck measured that, and the run went from stopping at RC-03 in 19 seconds to passing it and failing 640 seconds later for an unrelated reason. LIVE POPULATION, re-derived on the committed corpus with the disjunction-aware walker: 774 criteria examined; 0 of them (0.0%) name a field path in `requires`, so the PATHS rule -- the half RC-03's required contract actually named -- has an applicable population of ZERO and contributes no live assertion; 19 (2.5%) name a backticked phase of a related record, 22 tokens in all; 17 of those 19 rely on a waiver below, and all 17 waivers are in use; the remaining 5 tokens across 2 criteria (criterion.SalesAgreement.performed.v1: `delivered`, `discharged`, `transferred`; criterion.GrievanceCase.remedy_authorized.v1: `held`, `partly_consumed`) are bound by a conjunct and are the whole of the rule's live force. THE NARROW SCOPE IS THE ACCEPTED LIMIT, and the alternative was measured rather than argued. Widening the phase rule to unbackticked tokens of related records' phase vocabulary produces 425 findings across 266 of the 774 criteria (34%), over 62 distinct tokens -- case-sensitive, and already excluding every token a conjunct binds or a waiver excuses. The vocabulary is ordinary English past participles used as verbs: `recorded` 104 ("the subject's own declared identity/scope fields are recorded"), `required` 43 ("no judgment is required"), `current` 37, `admitted` 34, `assigned` 30 ("a custodian is assigned"). A waiver list of that size is not a waiver list, it is a second corpus, and a rule that demands one teaches contributors to route around the checker. So the rule keeps its scope, the number is written down here rather than left to be rediscovered, and what is added instead is the control the live half never had: fixtures/negative/r14-requires-names-a-related-phase-no-conjunct-binds. Until it, the only RC-03 fixture exercised the half with zero population. The cure for the formatting dependency is upstream and is not a checker change. A criterion's `requires` sentence and its conjuncts are written by one author in one entry of tools/phase_content.py, so what makes the rule reach is the author backticking the phases the sentence promises. That is a CONVENTION, nothing enforces it, and this sentence exists so that nobody reads the rule's name as though something did.

pinned_attachments_why:
F6D-01, and it is the SECOND half of a pin. A conjunct pin holds a guard to what its BODY must demand and says nothing about whether any edge CALLS it -- the file said so itself, one section down, about transitions. The measurement: one detachment fixture per guard, every call site removed, thirty runs, THIRTY UNDETECTED AND ZERO CAUGHT. Deleting `{"op":"call","predicate_id":"guard...."}` from an edge body is a one-line edit, the guard definition survives byte for byte, every conjunct pin still passes over it, and the whole apparatus reports green. Detaching two guards restores AT-M4-02; detaching one restores AS-X-01; detaching two restores the skill-grant path of R2 F-08.
This table is HAND-WRITTEN and is derived from nothing, for the same reason `pinned_transitions` is: a table computed from the registry it checks agrees with every edit to that registry. Each row names a guard and the exact edges that must call it, and the `why` says what detaching it restores -- a row whose reason is 'it should be attached' would be a row nobody can evaluate.
The check demands the call be DEMANDED, not merely present: a call inside a value slot, under a `not`, under an unopted disjunction or under a quantifier is a call the edge's truth does not depend on, which is the RC3-01/RC3-02 class one layer out. And every `guard.*` predicate in the registry must appear here exactly once, so a guard registered tomorrow with no attachment fails rather than arriving silently unattached.

pinned_attachments.why: An acceptance or a rejection with an empty resolution reason is the silent close section 9 row 14 refuses. Detached, both terminal edges of AcceptanceInterval accept an empty reason and the record still reads `accepted`.

Detached, work is admitted into a duty class whose acceptance role is unfilled -- R-X09's whole case, and section 9 row 12. The refusal has to happen at admission, because the moment the acceptance falls due is too late to staff it.

Detached, a refusal need name no failed predicate, and silence becomes refusal. This guard also carries the false-exclusion half -- unfamiliar wording is not a predicate -- so removing it loses the control in both directions at once.
Two edges, and both are needed: an approval with no expiry is a standing grant nobody renewed, on ExistenceJustification and on ProjectionGrant alike.
Detached, a model-authored typed value selects between acceptance strengths -- R-X19 and AS-M3-01 -- and the producing side picks how hard its own work will be checked.
Detached, a check interest's precondition reads fields the producer authored, so the producer decides whether it is checked.
Detached, the tie-break reverts to weakest-sufficient, which is the direction R-X20 exists to invert.

Detached, the derivation may declare an ordering and a rank returns. AT-M4-02 measured what that costs: one class computed from the set, one row applied, and C2's human requirement dropped on an action that is both C2 and C3. It is also the guard whose `unique` on reached_class_ids is what keeps the sibling gate check honest on the same edge.
Detached, the gate set may cover a proper subset of the reached set and the derivation still advances. This is the positive half of the same finding: no rank, AND every reached class gated.
Detached, a standing interest writes outside `proposed` -- it stops being a proposer and becomes an actor, with no admission in between.

AS-X-01, the round's only (d) landing on W5. Detached, the producing path authors the criteria its own work is accepted against. The review called the criteria pair the clearest close in the whole amendment; both halves live on one edge and both are one deletion away.
The other half: detached, criteria are amended between admission and submission, which is the same defeat arriving later.
Detached, the ordered custody resolver may return the admitting identity, so the party that admitted the work also holds custody of it (R-X06).
Detached, width is bounded by cost again and fifty sequential consultations each individually cheap sit inside one budget -- AS-X-04, and section 9 row 8.

Detached, `recomputed_at_release -> matched` asserts only that a recomputation happened. The release then proceeds on a set nobody compared to the admitted one, which is AT-M4-02 through the recompute path.
Two edges, and the second is the park route. Detached, the derivation is writable outside the release path and its append-only rule has nobody enforcing it.

Detached, a claim may precede its own allocation and the allocating component need not be C04 -- so the identity that is supposed to make a duplicate external effect detectable is written by whoever gets there first.
Detached, a step emits more than one effect and the step stops being the idempotency unit. Every retry story in section 6 rests on that being true.

F6D-11. Detached, `allocated -> claimed` asserts only that a claim happened, and the answer 05 section 6 gives to the protocol's tenth (d)-class example -- no stated winner between concurrent attempts on one work order -- is carried by nothing. The sibling guard is sound and is credited: it constrains ONE record's internal consistency, `allocated_at < claimed_at` and an allocating component of S1-C04, both of which are true of each racer independently.

F6D-06. Two admission edges, because both records declare the field. Detached, `declared_grants` is read by nothing again -- the string occurred in 0 predicate bodies when the review measured it -- and "a declared grant is resolved against the grant policy at admission" is a sentence about a resolution nobody performs. That is the decorative-declaration loophole the rule was written to close, reproduced by the rule: 44 capability declarations that nothing backed is the observed instance (R3 F57, F60).
Detached, a holder's stated minimum becomes consent rather than evidence, and a protected lane holder can refuse a shed outright -- AE-M4-01, section 9 row 9.
Two edges, `staffed` and `suspended`, because retirement is reachable from both. Detached, a holder retires while a duty it carries is live and the address the duty was routed to stops existing.

Detached, cap exhaustion refuses the next legitimate complainant instead of overflowing to a named destination with an alarm and a reader. R-X17's point is that the failure mode of an intake cap is silence toward the person with the grievance.

THE HARD RULE OF LAYER 3, and the layer's stated withdrawal condition is that it is violated. Detached, a standing interest's precondition invokes a model and the layer that exists to be deterministic is not.
Detached, an interest declares its own writer key, which is authority granting itself authority -- AS-M5-02.

Detached, the probe skill's arrival at the enforcement point stops being a failure, and grant REMOVAL loses the positive control that grant delivery has. With the sibling guard also detached the whole skill-grant path of R2 F-08 and R6 F7 is restored.

Nine edges, one per row of 08 section 1's table, and the count is the finding: before this, NO edge on any of the six control objects referenced `ProtectedChange` at all, and three of the six were not records. Detached from any one of them, the object that decides who may act, who is reachable for a duty or who may write a record changes through an ordinary transition owned by an ordinary component -- which is the W10 self-modification probe resolving the wrong way.

Detached, the loader's record no longer has to agree with the step's declaration, and negative control 6 -- an independent reviewer fed the producer's rationale -- is undetected at the one place the design says it is detected.

Detached, a reserved lane is released with no record of the lapsed unconsumed quantity, which is the quantity R-X24 says makes a never-consumed lane visible. Section 9 row 10 is the case: a reservation unconsumed at the lapse point, held past it.
Detached, a skill's declared tool grant stops being inert and the frontmatter grants tools for the turn that loads it -- the named runtime behaviour this rule was made structural to survive.
Detached, a supersession advances without walking the closure at all, so an accepted outcome standing on a superseded source is never reopened and nobody learns that it was not.
Detached, a derived item's trust level may exceed its inputs', which is laundering by derivation.
Detached, an activation re-reading its own output promotes it -- section 9 row 5, and the guard is the only thing that makes promotion an effect rather than a re-read.
